metadata.title: Warehouse Stewardship: Connective Tissue
metadata.notes: Essential skills for maintaining a living building during systemic infrastructure failure.

nodes.title: The Greywater Loop & Catchment
nodes.description: Surviving the dry taps. Building IBC tote rain catchments and gravity-fed sand/charcoal filtration. Wiring hydrostatic pressure sensors to monitor local reservoir levels.

nodes.title: The LoRaWAN Lifeline
nodes.description: Off-grid emergency communication. Building solar-powered LoRa radio nodes from scrap antennas. Transmitting semantic vectors during ISP/Cell blackouts.

nodes.title: Practical Consensus & The Proposal Ledger
nodes.description: Mediating warehouse disputes using Ubuntu layer math. Drafting resource requests for the mk0-fabricator and managing the local Isibaya voting cycles.

nodes.title: Polymer Sorting & The Detritivore Feed
nodes.description: Closing the material loop. Identifying scavenged plastics (ABS/PLA/PET) and preparing them for the mk0-detritivore without jamming or toxic fumes.

nodes.title: Warehouse Synesthesia (LED Mapping)
nodes.description: Translating the Thermodynamic Ledger into the physical environment. Mapping WS2812B strips to power/water telemetry for ambient building awareness.

nodes.title: The TEND-to-ZAR Liquidity Pool
nodes.description: Economic realism in Gauteng. Interfacing internal mutual credit with the external fiat economy by pooling warehouse physical outputs for ZAR trade.

nodes.title: The Autonomous Ark Capstone
nodes.description: Lead the warehouse through a simulated 'Total Failure' cycle (No grid, No water, No ISP). Successfully maintain all metabolic loops using only local mesh and reserves.

holonic_capstone.deliverable: 48 hours of autonomous operation data verified by the Mycelial Oracle and the Isibaya Council.

edges.rationale: Water level monitoring requires the ESP32 mesh skills learned in the handshake course.
Building radio nodes requires fundamental understanding of mesh networking.
An Ark cannot survive without sovereign water management.
Autonomous operation requires a resilient, long-range communication spine.
